hints: Because the load is lifted vertically at constant speed ($a = 0$), the lifting force balances the weight: $F = mg$.
Calculate the weight of the load: $W = 1250 \times 10 = 12500\text{ N}$.
Use the power formula $P = F \times V$ with $P = 20000\text{ W}$ and solve for $V$.
walkthrough:
Since the load moves vertically at constant speed, the acceleration is zero and the lifting force equals the weight of the load:
$$F = mg = 1250(10) = 12500\text{ N}$$

Apply the relationship between power, force, and velocity ($P = 20\text{ kW} = 20000\text{ W}$):
$$P = F \times V$$
$$20000 = 12500 \times V$$
$$V = \frac{20000}{12500} = 1.6\text{ m s}^{-1}$$
teacher_walkthrough:
State the vertical equilibrium condition for the load moving at constant speed ($a = 0$):
$$\Sigma F_y = 0 \implies F - mg = 0 \implies F = mg$$
Substitute $m = 1250\text{ kg}$ and $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$:
$$F = 1250 \times 10 = 12500\text{ N}$$

State the formula relating mechanical power to force and speed:
$$P = F \times V$$
Convert the crane's power from kilowatts to watts:
$$P = 20\text{ kW} = 20000\text{ W}$$

Substitute the known values and solve for the speed $V$:
$$20000 = 12500 \times V$$
Divide both sides by $12500$:
$$V = \frac{20000}{12500} = \frac{200}{125} = \frac{8}{5} = 1.6\text{ m s}^{-1}$$
